title: Format guardrail canary for JSON preservation on config/model changes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a lightweight canary test and monitoring pipeline that detects JSON formatting/regression (schema drift, type changes, missing keys, and subtle tokenization-induced format corruption) when model variants or serving config (quant, kernel, batching) change. The goal is a fast, low-cost safety net that runs on canary traffic and on pre-rollout smoke to surface formatting regressions before they reach most customers. This ticket covers design, an automated canary job, integration with evals and Console alerts, and a rollback trigger for flagged rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Canary job executes automatically for any model or config change in rollout pipeline and runs against a representative prompt set within <2 minutes of deployment start.

The canary pipeline computes a compact set of format signals: schema coverage, required-key presence ratio, strict JSON parse rate, field-type mismatch rate, and example-level fidelity score; thresholds are configurable per model.
Console shows a dedicated canary dashboard panel with per-rollout signal breakdown and a clear PASS/FAIL for the canary phase.
Automatic rollback hook fires and pauses rollout when the canary result fails the configured threshold and creates an incident in the rollout audit trail.
Canary outputs are persisted to the evals datastore with links to failed examples and token-level diffs for triage.
End-to-end latency overhead of the canary infrastructure on deployments is under 5% for average rollout time.
tasks: Design signal set and thresholds with Applied ML (list signals + recommended defaults)
Implement lightweight JSON parse/normalization library to catch subtle tokenization or escaping regressions
Build canary runner service that hooks into rollout API and triggers jobs for model/config changes
Integrate canary outputs with evals datastore and attach example artifacts to rollout records
Add Console UI panel and alert rules for canary PASS/FAIL and signal-level trends
Wire automatic rollback hook and workflow with on-call and PRD playbook links
implementation_notes: Prefer using existing evals harness and example corpus to avoid duplicating heavy datasets
Run canary on a small, deterministic prompt corpus (50-200 prompts) that targets structured-output patterns used by customers
Use strict JSON parsing plus a normalization pass (key ordering agnostic, canonical whitespace removal) before diffing
Produce both aggregate metrics and failing example payloads with token-level annotations for blame assignment
Thresholds should be configurable per model and overrideable per-customer for enterprise Dedicated/Private deployments
